 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition are as under:
That on 19.02.2019 at about 9.30 p.m., when the Petitioner was driving an Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-42-4243 and reached near Madappa house, Bhommachanahalli village, SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 Kasaba Hobli, Ramanagara Taluk, at that time,
the driver of the Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA-7941 driven in a very rash and negligent manner and suddenly applied brake.
Due to which, the Petitioner's auto hit to the Swaraj Mazada vehicle.
Due to the said impact, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

Immediately, after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Ramakrishna Hospital,
Ramanagara, wherein the Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.
The Petitioner had spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was a driver and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA-7941 by its driver.
The Respondent No.1 is the Owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA-7941.
Therefore, both the SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
4. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement.

5. The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.

Further it contended that it has issued Liability only policy in favour of the offending vehicle which had been canceled prior to the date of the accident, since, the Cheque which was issued by the owner / Respondent No.1 towards payment of premium amount was dishonoured.
Therefore, it has duly canceled the aforesaid policy for non-compliance of 64-VB of Insurance Act 1938.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Sathisha.

H vs Manjunatha R.K on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86956171/
2 SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the rival Pleadings, my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that on 19.02.2019 at about 9.30 p.m., when he was riding Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-42- 4243, reached near Madappa house, Bhommachanahalli village, Kasaba Hobli, the driver of the Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA-7941 has drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly applied the brake as a result, his Auto hit the Swaraj Mazda vehicle and he has sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the claim petition?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed?

If so, from whom and what is the quantum?
3) What Order or Award?
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 9 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-9.
Further, the Petitioner has examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P10 & 11 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.2 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 & 2 and got marked 7 documents at Ex.R1 to 7 and closed its side evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order for the following :

REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 occurred due to the sudden application of brake by the driver of the offending Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA- 7941.
Sathisha.H vs Manjunatha R.K on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86956171/
3 10.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident occurred by the driver of the offending Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA-7941.
11.

In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 9 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-9 and he has re-iterated the Petition averments in his Chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-9 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar, IMV Report,
Wound Certificate, Charge sheet, Aadhaar card, Discharge summary and Hospital and Medical bill.

12. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P- 1 & 2 are the True copies of the FIR &
Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by the mother of the Petitioner by name Smt.

Lakshmamma W/o Late Hanumaiah, the SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 Ramanagara Rural Police have registered the case against the driver of the Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA-7941 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the true copy of Spot Mahazar which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner which shows that he had sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P.6 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which has been submitted by the PSI of the Ramanagara Rural Police Station against the driver of the offending Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA-7941 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P7 is the Aadhaar card.
Ex.P8 is the Discharge summary.
Ex.P9 is the Hospital and Medical bills.

Further, the Petitioner has examined doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.10 & 11.
14.
P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Official by name Shreyas Bhat as RW.1 and got marked 6 documents at Ex.R1 to 5 and 7.
But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contention of the Petitioner regarding accident.

The IMV report clearly shows that the damages found on the front of the Auto and the damages to the back side of the offending vehicle which clearly corroborate the version of the Petitioner regarding accident.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA-7941 by its driver and the sudden application of brake, due to which the SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 accident had occurred and he had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 32 years.
The Petitioner has produced his Aadhaar card at Ex.P7 which shows his date of birth as 31.03.1987.

The accident has taken place on Sathisha.H vs Manjunatha R.K on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86956171/
4 19.02.2019.
Hence, at the time of accident, the Petitioner was aged about 31 years, 10 months and 18 days.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner to be taken at 32 years for the purpose of assessment.

17. In the petition, the Petitioner has stated that he was a driver and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/-
per month.
But, he has not produced any document in respect of income.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 to be taken at Rs.14,000/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :

19 . The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-5 issued by the Ramakrishna Hospital, shows that in the said accident the Petitioner had sustained following injuries:
1) CLW (6cm) over right frontal region 2) CLW (1cm) over philttum 3) Right eye sub conjunctional haemontage 4) Displaced fracture shaft of right femur 5) CLW (4cm) left knee - pre patellar region 6) IDK left knee - Anteromedial instability SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 As per the opinion of the Doctor, said injuries are grievous in nature.
20. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of 40,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
21. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 25,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
22.

The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at Ramakrishna Hospital,
Ramanagara.

Upon going through Ex.P.8 - Discharge summary of Ramakrishna Hospital,
Ramanagara, shows that the Petitioner was admitted SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 as an inpatient in the said hospital from 19.02.2019 to 26.02.2019.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 8 days.

Sathisha.H vs Manjunatha R.K on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86956171/
5 23.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 28,000/- under this head (@ 14,000/- per month ).
IV.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :

24. Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 6,000/- (@ 100/- per day) towards attendants charges, 6,000/- towards extra diet and SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 nourishment and 6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
25. The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced medical bills at Ex.P9 totally amounting to Rs.68,257/-.
I have gone through the same and the same is acceptable.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.68,300/-.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.68,300/- under this head.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:

26. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

27. Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him at Ramakrishna Hospital, Ramanagara.
Further, he assessed the disability to Right Lower Limb at 46% and whole body disability of the Petitioner at 15%.
PW.2 got marked Clinical Notes and X-ray at Ex.P10 and 11.
In the cross-examination, he deposed that he has not treated the Petitioner and he did not get the opinion of the treated doctor.
He admitted that the fracture of the Petitioner is united and now there is no problem in the said place.
He further admitted that the Petitioner does not have problem from the implants.
He further admitted that he has not issued estimation for further treatment.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8% would be just and proper.
28. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 16.

With multiplier of 16, income of 14,000/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to Sathisha.H vs Manjunatha R.K on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86956171/
6

his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to 2,15,040/- (14,000/- x 12 = 1,68,000/-,
1,68,000/-x 16 x 8/100 =2,15,040/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 2,15,040/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
29.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  40,000 /-
2. Loss of amenities  25,000/-
 SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 3. Loss of income during the laid  28,000/-
 up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  18,000/-
 and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  68,300/-
6. Loss of Future Income 2,15,040/-
 Total 3,94,340/-
30.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 3,94,340/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

31. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending Swaraj Mazada bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AA-7941.

In this case, the Respondent No.2 being the insurer has taken contention that it has issued a Liability only policy in favour of the Respondent No.1 in respect of the offending vehicle which had been canceled prior to the date of the accident, since, the Cheque which was issued by the Owner / Respondent No.1 SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 towards payment of premium amount was dishonored.
Therefore, it has duly canceled the said policy for non compliance of 64 VB of Insurance Act 1938.
Therefore, there was no subsistence of contract of insurance between the Respondent No.1 and it as on the date of the accident.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

The Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied on the decision reported in 2012(1) AIR Kar R 65 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Srinivasa Subbanna and another, wherein the Sathisha.H vs Manjunatha R.K on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86956171/
7

sentences.text:
Hon'ble High Court of Karanataka has pleased to held that:
"Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 1988), S.147 - Compensation - Liability of Insurer - Cheque issued by insured towards payment of premium was dishonoured

- insured /
owner was duly served with notice about cancellation of policy on account thereof,
much before accident occurred - No privity of contract between owner and insurer - insurer not liable to pay compensation and recover same from owner (paras 10, 12)."
32.
In order to substantiate its contention, it has examined its Manager by name Shreyas Bhat as RW.1 and he SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 has reiterated the said fact in his chief-affidavit.
He got marked 6 documents at Ex.R1 to 5 and 7 i.e., Authorization letter, Original Cheque, Cancellation Letter, Bank Return Memo, List of Post Article, Certified Copy of Policy.
The Respondent No.2 has also examined the Assistant Manager of Panjab National Bank by name Padmavathi as RW.2 and she got marked one document at Ex.P6.
In the cross-examination RW.1 has deposed that the validity of the Policy it has issued is subject to the realization of the Cheque.

Upon going through Ex.R2 i.e.,
Original Cheque bearing No.429949 dated 02.03.2018 for Rs.27,123/- in favour of the Respondent No.2 shows it has issued towards the premium of policy.
Ex.R4 is the Bank Return Memo dated 21.03.2018 shows that on presentation of said Cheque for encashment, the same was returned with an endorsement as "Funds insufficient."

Ex.R5 is the Notice issued by the Respondent No.2 to the Respondent No.1 stating that the payment of premium against the policy vide Cheque No.429949 of Punjab National Bank for an SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 amount of Rs.27,123/- could not be honored and the Cheque has been returned for the reason funds insufficient.
Further, the Respondent No.2 has issued Notice to the Respondent No.1 informing the cancellation of policy and it is not responsible for any liability.

So, this Notice was issued to the Respondent No.1 clearly shows that the Respondent No.2 has canceled the policy which it has issued to the Respondent No.1 in respect of the offending vehicle since, the payment of premium against the said policy vide Cheque was dishonored for funds insufficient.
The Notice issued to the Respondent No.1 was duly served on 10.04.2018.
Ex.R6 is the Statement of Account which got marked through RW.2 shows that as on 21.03.2018 there is no sufficient balance in the account of Respondent No.1.

However, the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner cross- examined RW.2 and suggested that Cheque No.429949 for Rs.27,123/- was credited to Tata AIG general Insurance Company and same was admitted by RW.2.

In the chief- examination RW.2 has deposed that as on 21.03.2018 there SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 was no sufficient balance in the account of Respondent No1 and there was SMS Alert to the Account holder in respect of balance amount and the message was sent to the Account holder for Cheque bounce.
It is pertinent to note here that Ex.R5 is the Notice for cancellation of policy which was dated 06.04.2018 and Cheque on presentation was returned for Funds insufficient dated 21.03.2018.
Ex . R6

- Account Statement shows an amount of Rs.27,123/- was credited to Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd., through the Cheque bearing No.429950 dated 13.03.2018 which is prior to the issuance of Notice of cancellation and prior to the date of presentation of the Cheque which was issued in respect of premium to the present policy.

entities.text: Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So, it is clear that the said Cheque bearing No.429950 and amount was not in respect of the present policy and vehicle.
The alleged accident has been occurred on 19.02.2018.

Though, the Notice of cancellation of policy was issued on 06.04.2018, since, from then till the date of accident i.e., 19.02.2018, the Respondent No.1 has not paid SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 the premium amount.

So, there is no privity of contract between Sathisha.H vs Manjunatha R.K on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86956171/
8 the Respondent No.1 and 2.
Therefore, the Respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
33. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.

The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of 3,94,340/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum SCCH 15 MVC No.2081/2019 from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the owner, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
